title: The work breakdown structure
blurb: Describe the work breakdown structure, how it links the product breakdown structure to work packages, and how it helps the project manager organize teams.
question: What is the work breakdown structure, and how does it help the project manager?

teach.h: A hierarchy of all the work
teach.body: Formally: the work breakdown structure (WBS) is a hierarchy of all the work to be done during a project, forming a link between the product breakdown structure and the work packages. It supports the project manager in deciding how to structure project teams and the boundaries between them. In plain English: list every piece of work needed to make the products, group it sensibly, and you can see who should do what.

teach.h: Why organizing cares about the WBS
teach.body: How the work is broken down shapes the teams. Group work cleanly and each team has a clear boundary and a clear manager; group it badly and teams overlap or leave gaps. The WBS also shapes the design of the project ecosystem and, through the commercial management approach, shows which parts of the work external suppliers will deliver.

head: Place
Role of the WBS
rows: Shapes how work and people are organized
Delivery model: WBS parts for external suppliers

teach.body: Ravensby Borough Council is building a community library. Project manager Femi Adeyemi starts from the product breakdown structure (building, catalogue system, trained staff) and works out all the work needed to make each one. The WBS shows three natural groups: building works for the construction contractor, digital services for the council's IT team, and opening activities for the library service. Femi uses those boundaries to set up three teams, each under its own team manager.

teach.text: Trap: the WBS is NOT the product breakdown structure. The PBS lists products; the WBS lists all the work, linking the products to work packages. Nor is it the PMT structure, which charts people and roles.

items: WBS: a hierarchy of all work to be done in the project.
It links the product breakdown structure to the work packages.
It helps the PM decide how to structure teams and their boundaries.
The commercial management approach can use it to show what external suppliers deliver.

summary: You can now define the work breakdown structure, contrast it with the product breakdown structure and the PMT structure, and explain how it helps the project manager organize teams and suppliers.

A.q: What is a work breakdown structure?
options: A hierarchy of all products to be produced in it
A chart of the people in management roles
A hierarchy of all work done during the project
A diagram of the sequence of the project products
A.why: The WBS is a hierarchy of all work to be done during the project (6.2.5).

whyNot.0: A hierarchy of products is the product breakdown structure.
whyNot.1: A chart of people in management roles is the project management team structure.
whyNot.3: The sequence of products is shown in the product flow diagram.

A.q: Which two things does the work breakdown structure link?
options: The business case and the project plan
The PBS and the work packages
The risk register and the issue register
The project mandate and the project brief
A.why: The WBS forms a link between the product breakdown structure and the work packages.

whyNot.0: The project plan supports the business case, but that is not the WBS link.
whyNot.2: Both registers are parts of the project log; the WBS does not link them.
whyNot.3: The project brief is built from the mandate in starting up; the WBS plays no part.

A.q: How does the WBS help the project manager?
options: Choosing responses to the threats on the project
Setting the stage tolerances for the board
Forecasting which benefits users will realize
Deciding how to structure teams and their boundaries
A.why: The WBS supports the PM in deciding how to structure project teams and the boundaries between them.

whyNot.0: Choosing threat responses belongs to the risk practice.
whyNot.1: Stage tolerances are set by the board, not derived from the WBS.
whyNot.2: Benefits forecasting is a business case matter for the senior user and executive.

B.q:
Which two statements about the work breakdown structure are correct?
1. It breaks down all the work, not just the products.
2. It is another name for the PMT structure.
3. It can show which parts of the work external suppliers deliver.
4. It removes the need for work packages.
B.why: The WBS covers all the work (1), and the commercial management approach's delivery model can name WBS elements delivered by external suppliers (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: the PMT structure charts roles and people, not work.
whyNot.1: Both are false: the WBS is not the PMT structure, and it links to work packages rather than replacing them.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: the WBS links products to work packages.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In product-based planning, the WBS, estimates and schedule are derived from the [?] descriptions.
B.why: Product-based planning starts from products and derives the WBS, estimates and schedule from the product descriptions.

whyNot.1: Role descriptions describe responsibilities in the PMT, not the work.
whyNot.2: Stage plans are built from products, not from 'stage descriptions'.
whyNot.3: PRINCE2 has no separate quality descriptions; quality specifications sit inside the product descriptions.

B.q: Lessons from an earlier project are used to shape the WBS for a new one. Which principle is the organizing practice applying?
B.why: The organizing practice applies learn from experience by using lessons to inform the PMT structure, the WBS and a healthy project ecosystem (tab 6.5).

whyNot.0: Manage by stages is applied by adapting the structure at stage boundaries.
whyNot.2: Focus on products is about defining products and their descriptions.
whyNot.3: Tailoring is applied by creating a PMT suited to the project and the people involved, not by using lessons.

C.q: During initiation the project manager develops the product breakdown structure and the WBS. Which process is this, and which practice does the official guidance say is being applied?
C.why: In initiating a project, the plans practice is applied by developing the PBS, WBS and product flow diagram (tab 15.3).

whyNot.0: Starting up plans only the initiation stage; the project-level PBS and WBS come in initiation.
whyNot.1: The process is right, but developing the PBS and WBS applies the plans practice.
whyNot.3: Controlling a stage runs delivery stages; the WBS is developed in initiation.

C.q: A council will use an external contractor for all building work. Where should this be described, and what identifies that block of work?
C.why: The commercial management approach's delivery model describes which WBS elements external suppliers will deliver.

whyNot.1: The communication management approach covers stakeholder communication, not supplier delivery.
whyNot.2: The quality management approach covers quality methods and responsibilities, and the PBS lists products, not work.
whyNot.3: The project brief is a start-up product, and the PMT structure charts roles, not work.

C.q: Which statement correctly contrasts the PBS and the WBS?
options: PBS lists the work; WBS lists the products it makes
PBS lists the people; WBS lists their tasks
PBS lists the stages; WBS lists the risks in each
PBS lists products; WBS lists the work to make them
C.why: The PBS is a hierarchy of products; the WBS is a hierarchy of all the work, linking those products to work packages.

whyNot.1: People and roles are shown in the PMT structure, not the PBS.
whyNot.2: Neither structure is a list of stages or risks.

reteach.title: Planning a wedding: things versus jobs
reteach.question: For a wedding, is 'the cake' the same as 'bake, decorate and deliver the cake'?

blocks.h: Products and the work behind them
blocks.body: A list of things the wedding needs (venue, cake, flowers) is like the product breakdown structure. A list of all the jobs needed to get them (book venue, bake cake, decorate, deliver, arrange flowers) is like the WBS. Grouping those jobs shows who should do what: the baker's team, the florist's team. Those groups become work packages.

blocks.text: The WBS is about work, not products: 'the cake' is a product; 'bake the cake' is work.

explain.body: The WBS is a hierarchy of all work to be done during a project.

test.q: The work breakdown structure is a hierarchy of what?
test.why: The WBS is a hierarchy of all work to be done during the project.

whyNot.0: Roles are shown in the PMT structure.
whyNot.2: Products are shown in the product breakdown structure.
whyNot.3: Stages are set out in the project plan.

explain.body: The WBS links the product breakdown structure to the work packages handed to teams.

test.q: What does the WBS lead to, for handing to team managers?
test.why: The WBS forms a link between the product breakdown structure and the work packages.

whyNot.0: Stage plans are prepared by the PM for the board, not handed to team managers.
whyNot.2: Highlight reports go from the PM to the board.

explain.body: The WBS supports the PM in deciding how to structure project teams and the boundaries between them.

test.q: Which use of the WBS supports the organizing practice?
options: Structuring teams and the boundaries between teams
Setting the quality tolerances for each product
Recording issues raised against the baselines
Forecasting the benefits expected after closure
test.why: Organizing uses the WBS to decide how to structure teams and their boundaries.

whyNot.1: Quality tolerances come from acceptance criteria and quality specifications.
whyNot.2: Issues are recorded in the issue register under the issues practice.
whyNot.3: Post-project benefits are tracked through the benefits management approach.

explain.body: The commercial management approach has a delivery model heading that describes which WBS elements external suppliers will deliver.

test.q: Which heading of the commercial management approach can name the WBS elements to be delivered by external suppliers?
test.why: The delivery model heading describes the delivery model, for example which WBS elements external suppliers will deliver.

whyNot.0: Resources covers the people for market engagement, procurement and contract management.
whyNot.1: Responsibilities covers who does market engagement, procurement and contract management.
whyNot.3: Stakeholder analysis belongs to the communication management approach.
